newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to cut mobile phone interconnection charges.
newsitem.headline: Italy to cut mobile phone interconnection charges.

text.p: Italy's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said it had defined a reduction of interconnection charges for mobile phone operators.

A Ministry statement gave no details but quoted Undersecretary Michele Lauria as saying this was "a further important step towards the complete liberalisation of the telecommunications sector forecast for January 1, 1998."

This measure, Lauria said, was not just limited to a reduction in tariffs "but outlines a route along which the operators -- Telecom Italia, Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and (Olivetti -controlled) Omnitel Pronto Italia -- will have to move in coming months for major and transparent action to support regulations with the aim of carrying out further reviews by the end of the year."

The Ministry intended to continue to carry out its "delicate role as referee in the process of liberalisation that is under way," while ensuring that consumers got the full benefit of price reductions, the statement said.
It said the list of interconnection charges would be published by Telecom Italia on July 1.

European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has been highly critical of the so-called interconnection fees charged by Italian state telecoms group Stet -- which until recently enjoyed a monopoly -- to operators in return for access to its network.
He said in Rome last month that the interconnection charges in Italy were currently more than double the average in the European Union.
The Commission had set a deadline of July 1 this year for all EU telecoms operators to publish tariffs and conditions governing interconnection.
